```{r, results="hide", echo=FALSE}
if (!exists(".version")) {
```

```{r, results="asis", echo=FALSE}
cat("# Compressed sparse matrix (", as.character(.version), ")", sep="")
```

## Overview

The `compressed_sparse_matrix` specification describes an on-disk representation of a **compressed sparse matrix**.
This can use either the compressed sparse row (CSR) or compressed sparse column (CSC) format.

## Object metadata

The `OBJECT` file should contain a `compressed_sparse_matrix` property, itself a JSON object with the following properties:

- `version`, a string specifying the version of the `compressed_sparse_matrix` format.
```{r, results="asis", echo=FALSE}
cat("  This should be set to \"", as.character(.version), "\".", sep="")
```

## Directory structure

### Contents 

The directory should contain the following:

- `OBJECT`, a JSON file as described above.
- `matrix.h5`, a HDF5 file.

### `matrix.h5`

#### Basic

The `matrix.h5` file should contain an `compressed_sparse_matrix` group.

The `compressed_sparse_matrix` group should have a `layout` scalar string attribute.
The attribute value should either be `"CSR"` or `"CSC"`, specifying whether the matrix is compressed sparse row or column, respectively.

The `compressed_sparse_matrix` group should contain `shape`, a 1-dimensional dataset of any datatype that is representable by a 64-bit unsigned integer.
This dataset should have length 2 where the entries specify the number of rows and columns, respectively, of the matrix.

The `compressed_sparse_matrix` group should have a `type` scalar string attribute, specifying the data type of the sparse matrix.
The attribute value should either be `"integer"`, `"boolean"` or `"number"`. 

#### Data

The `compressed_sparse_matrix` group should contain `data`, a 1-dimensional dataset containing the values of the structural non-zero elements in the **compressed sparse matrix**.
The length of this dataset defines the number of structural non-zero elements. 
The set of acceptable HDF5 datatypes of this dataset depends on `type`:

- For `type = "integer"` or `"boolean"`, the datatype should be representable by a 32-bit signed integer.
- For `type = "number"`, the datatype should be representable by a 64-bit float.

Note that structural non-zero elements are allowed to have a value of zero, i.e., non-structural zeros may still be present.

Optionally, the `compressed_sparse_matrix/data` dataset may have a `missing-value-placeholder` scalar attribute. 
The datatype of the attribute should be the same as the dataset.
All entries in the dataset equal to the placeholder should be treated as missing.

#### Indices

The `compressed_sparse_matrix` group should contain an `indices` dataset.
This is a 1-dimensional dataset containing the 0-based row indices (for CSC) or column indices (for CSR) for the structural non-zero elements.
It should have a datatype that is representable by a 64-bit unsigned integer.
The length of the `compressed_sparse_matrix/indices` dataset should be equal to the number of structural non-zero elements in the `compressed_sparse_matrix/data` dataset,
i.e., the $i$-th entry of the former contains the row/column index for the $i$-th structural non-zero element in the latter.
All entries should be less than the number of rows (for CSC) or columns (for CSR), as defined by the `compressed_sparse_matrix/shape` dataset.

The `compressed_sparse_matrix` group should contain an `indptr` dataset.
This is a 1-dimensional dataset containing the pointer offsets for the columns (for CSC) or rows (for CSR).
The length of this dataset should be equal to the number of columns plus 1 (for CSC) or the number of rows plus 1 (for CSR).
It should have a datatype that is representable by a 64-bit unsigned integer.
The first entry of the dataset should be zero while the last entry should be equal to the number of structural non-zero elements in the `compressed_sparse_matrix/data` dataset.
Entries of this dataset should be sorted in non-strictly increasing order.

The structural non-zero elements belonging to the $i$-th column (for CSC) or row (for CSR) are located by the slice $[P_i, P_{i+1})$,
where $P_i$ and $P_{i+1}$ are the $i$-th and $i+1$-th elements of the `compressed_sparse_matrix/indptr` dataset, respectively.
These should be interpreted as pointers into the `compressed_sparse_matrix/indices` and `compressed_sparse_matrix/data` datasets,
i.e., the first structural non-zero element in row/column $i$ is the $P_i$-th entry of those datasets,
while the $P_{i+1}$-th entry is the position immediately after the last structural non-zero element of that row/column.
The indices of the structural non-zeros for a given row/column should be sorted in strictly increasing order,
i.e., $I_{P_i} < I_{P_i + 1} < ... < I_{P_{i+1} - 1}$ where $I_j$ is the $j$-th entry of the `compressed_sparse_matrix/indices` dataset.

#### Names

Optionally, the `compressed_sparse_matrix` group may contain a `names` group.
This may contain any number of 1-dimensional string datasets named after the corresponding dimension,
i.e., the `compressed_sparse_matrix/names/{d}` dataset corresponds to the $d$-th dimension.
Each dataset contains the names for its dimension and should have a length equal to the extent of that dimension.

Aside from the aforementioned datasets, no other objects should be present in the `compressed_sparse_matrix/names` group.

## Height

The height of the **compressed sparse matrix** is defined as the number of rows, as specified in the `compressed_sparse_matrix/shape` dataset of `matrix.h5`.

## Dimensions

The dimensions of the **compressed sparse matrix** are taken from the `compressed_sparse_matrix/shape` dataset of `matrix.h5`.
